newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to auction share portfolio on December 30.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to auction share portfolio on December 30.

text.p: The Brazilian federal government will auction on December 30 a portfolio of minority shares in a variety of companies including Telebras, an official at Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said.
"It will be a small auction on December 30 within the framework of the national privatization plan (PND)," BNDES vice-president and director of privatizations Jose Pio Borges told reporters.
"It will be a number of shares in companies like (federal telecommunications giant) Telebras and (state power firm) Cemig, worth around 30 million reais ($28.8 million)," he added.
Borges did not say which other companies would be included in the sale nor what percentage of the federal government's holding in these firms would be sold off in the auction.

He added that the Minas Gerais region was likely to start the bidding process for a 33 percent stake of Companhia de Eletricidade de Minas Gerais (Cemig) in January rather than in December, as originally scheduled.
Telebras, Latin America's largest phone company, is scheduled to be dismantled and sold off by the end of 1998.

The government opened the telecommunications sector to private capital earlier this week with the sale of a strategic 35 percent stake in state telecom Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT).
Borges said federal privatisation receipts were $4 billion in 1996, while at state level the sell-off of CRT and Rio de Janeiro power utility Cerj had raised $1.24 billion.
Brazil has said it hopes to boost revenue from federal privatisations to more than $10 billion in 1997.
